beats.text: Four dollars That is what it costs to start fixing a musty
house Not four hundred Not the price of a dehumidifier
Four dollars and most of it goes to something your grandfather could
buy at the hardware store in nineteen fifty I am talking
about the damp that makes your basement smell like a wet dog The
must that settles into your closets The little gray spots
of mold on a corner of the ceiling that you have been politely not seeing
for a year You have probably been told the answer is a two-hundred-dollar
machine that runs all summer and eats electricity
That is not the old way The old way was cheaper It was simpler
And it started with one honest question Where is the water coming from
Here is what damp air is actually costing you A dehumidifier
big enough to do anything useful costs a hundred and fifty
to three hundred dollars and then it runs every single day
Every day it runs it pulls power out of your wall And
a machine that sits in the corner is not fixing anything It
is working around the problem and it never stops working because
the problem never goes away Then there is the mold The
EPA says roughly half of all homes in this country
have had a dampness or mold problem at some point Half
And when the mold gets a real foothold in a basement the fix
stops being a bucket and starts being a crew A professional
mold remediation job runs fifteen hundred to six thousand
dollars depending on how far it got And you cannot see
most of it Damp air does its damage behind the wall
under the floor in the back of the closet where you never look That
is the part that worries me most Not the smell The part
you cannot see Nobody in my grandfather's day bought a machine
to dry out their basement They did something smarter They
kept the water out in the first place Think about an old
farmhouse cellar It was cold It was dry It
kept the potatoes through the winter and the jars on the shelf never
grew a beard And nobody in that house ever paid for
a dehumidifier because there was no such thing So
how was it dry Look at the house before you look at the cellar The
ground around it sloped away from the foundation The
gutters ran the rainwater twenty feet from the wall before
it ever hit the dirt The cellar windows sat above grade
and opened in the summer The house could breathe and the water
never got a chance to come in That is the forgotten fix You
do not dry a wet house You stop the house from getting wet
Every machine in the world will not save you if the water keeps
coming in faster than you can pull it out So step one
before you spend a dime on anything walk around the outside
of your house This takes ten minutes and it costs nothing
Look at the gutters first Are they full Is water
overflowing the edge during a rain and running straight down the
wall That is a free firehose pointed at your foundation
Clean them out or have them cleaned and make sure the downspouts
dump water at least six to ten feet away from the house They
sell little plastic extensions for a couple of dollars or
you can point the downspout at the driveway Then look at the ground
Does the dirt slope toward the house or away It needs
to slope away A foot of fall in ten feet is plenty
If the grade dips against the foundation water sits right
there and pushes into the wall Add dirt and pack it down
This is free While you are out there look at the window wells
A basement window well that fills with leaves and water is
a puddle pressed against the glass and the water will work its
way around the frame Keep them clean and if water sits
in them drill a little drain hole in the bottom and fill
it with gravel Ten minutes of work And check the sump pump
if you have one Make sure it is plugged in make sure it runs
when the water comes A dead sump pump is the most expensive
free problem you will ever ignore Now for the
damp that is already inside here is the four dollar fix
It is a tub of calcium chloride The same stuff they sell
in the ice melt aisle in winter The same active ingredient
in those little plastic moisture absorber tubs you see in the hardware
store except you are buying it for a fraction of the price
Here is what it does Calcium chloride is a desiccant
It pulls water out of the air and holds onto it You put
it in a container leave the top open and set it in the damp
spot In a week you will see water collected in
the bottom of that container Water that was in the air Water
that was going to be somebody's mold Now a few details
on how to set it up because the difference between works and barely
works is in the setup Use a container that holds the tub
up off the bottom or one that has a drip hole and a
catch tray so the water drains away from the salt instead
of drowning it The salt does its job by staying dry on top
and dropping the water below If the salt sits in its own water
it stops pulling That is the whole secret and it
is why the cheap plastic tubs you can buy have that little grate inside
You are building the same thing for less money Put the container
where the damp air can reach it not tucked behind a box
Air has to move across the open top for it to work The musty
closet The bathroom vanity with the damp pipes underneath
The crawl space The back corner of the laundry room The
attic access The places where you can smell it One
tub per small space What you do not do is leave it open
where a kid or a pet can reach it Put it up high or
in a cabinet or behind a latch And when the tub fills
with water do not pour it on your plants The salt
is concentrated in that water and it will kill them Pour
it down a drain throw the tub away and set a fresh one
A tub lasts six to eight weeks in a normal damp spot
and it costs about four dollars You will replace it maybe six
times a year That is less than the electricity for one
month of a dehumidifier Here is the part nobody wants
to hear Half of indoor damp is made by the people living
in the house Your dryer is the big one If your dryer
is vented inside into the laundry room or
into a bucket of water like some apartments do you are pumping
gallons of water into your house with every load That
dryer vent belongs outside If it is already outside
check that the hose is not pinched or disconnected Cooking
without a vent fan sends a load of steam into the air
Shower steam does the same These are not problems you have to live
with You just have to move them out A bathroom fan
for twenty minutes after a shower the vent fan on while
you cook the window cracked in the kitchen in the summer Small
habits and they add up to gallons a week And here is an
old one Laundry on a line hung indoors
will wet your house down like a rainstorm Damp clothes give
up their water into the air and your walls pick it up If
you line dry do it outside or in a garage with
the door cracked The old farmhouse way was to dry clothes
on a line in the sun not in the middle of the living room Still
air is what mold loves You can fix half of a damp problem
by making the air move The old houses did this with windows
and the stack effect Cool night air is drier than warm day
air In the summer open the windows on the shady side
at night and let the house flush itself out Even
one window open in a damp basement screened will
change that room Inside the house keep the air moving
on the cheap Closet doors open a crack instead of sealed
shut Furniture six inches off the wall so the wall
can breathe A ceiling fan on low in the damp room
not for you but for the air The science is simple Wet
air that sits still becomes wet walls Wet air that moves
becomes a memory One more piece of air movement and
it is the one people skip The vents in your foundation the
little screened holes in the crawl space wall They are not decoration
They are the house breathing If you have sealed them up or stacked
boxes against them or the previous owner did unblock
them A crawl space that cannot breathe is a mold machine
and it does not care how many buckets you put inside it So you
have stopped the water You have pulled the damp out of the air Now
you have to deal with what already grew On hard surfaces
tile glass plastic a bucket of detergent
and water with a scrub brush will do the job Soap lifts
mold off you wipe it done Rinse and dry it after
Do not reach for the bleach The EPA is clear on this
and it surprises people Bleach does not soak into porous
materials On drywall and wood bleach
treats the surface and leaves the mold alive underneath where
it will come right back That is why the mold you bleached last
spring is back this fall It was never dead And
here is the hard truth If the mold is on drywall or
on wood that has been wet for a while you do not clean it You
cut it out and replace it That sounds like bad news and
it is but it is honest news The mold is in
the material The material is done Cut it out fix
the water and put in a new piece and it will not come back
Now the questions I know you are asking because I have been fixing
damp houses long enough to hear them all Does a four dollar
bucket really do anything Here is my honest answer In
a small space a closet a vanity a crawl
space a car yes You will see water
in the bottom of the tub in a week That is not magic
that is chemistry But it will not dry out a whole open basement
by itself That is not what it is for For a whole
basement you do step one the water outside
and step four the air moving If you still need a machine
after that get the machine The bucket is not a replacement
for a dehumidifier in a big space It is a replacement
for the corner of the house where a dehumidifier would be overkill
Is calcium chloride safe It is a salt and concentrated
it can irritate skin and eyes and it is not something a pet
should lick Keep it out of reach up high or latched
The liquid that collects is concentrated too so it goes
down a drain not on the lawn Common sense same
as bleach or any cleaner you already own Will the mold
come back if I just use the bucket Yes And I am glad
you asked because that is the whole point of this video If
the water keeps coming in the mold will keep coming back
and no bucket no machine no spray will
ever win that fight The bucket buys you time The
gutters and the grade and the dryer vent win the fight What
if I live somewhere humid Then the bucket works better not
worse The more water in the air the more the desiccant
pulls You will change it more often Same fix
What about the dehumidifier I already own Do not throw
it away I am not here to tell you machines are evil A
dehumidifier is a real tool for a genuinely wet
house The point is not the machine The point is
that the machine should be the last thing you buy not the first
Do the ten minute walk fix the dryer vent unblock
the vents put out the buckets and then see what is left
Most people find there is nothing left to buy And one question I get
a lot Does the bucket smell The tub itself will start
to smell like a wet basement if you let it sit full of water
for weeks That is why you check it every couple of weeks
and change it when it fills A tub that you tend is a tool A
tub that you forget is a science experiment This works
in more places than a house That musty car that smells
like a damp towel every time you get in it One tub
under the seat for a week and the smell is gone A boat
a camper a shed a storage unit the back
of a closet in an apartment Anywhere small and still
and damp the same four dollar tub does the same job
If you rent you cannot fix the grade or the gutters and
I am not going to pretend you can You can still do the bucket the
fans the venting habits and the open closet doors
You can do a lot with four dollars and a window A couple more
places people never think to look A gun safe or
a toolbox or a footlocker in the garage where the damp
gets in and the smell stays One small container
of the same salt and the inside of that box stays dry
through a humid summer A pair of boots in the closet a
duffel in the attic a suitcase under the bed Same
idea same four dollars and you will stop smelling
your own closets And if your basement is genuinely wet
standing water wet do not buy a bucket of salt and
call it a day That is a different animal You need the sump
the gutters the grading maybe a French drain and
yes probably a machine Start with the water outside
That rule does not change So here is the whole thing in one
breath Four dollars A tub of calcium chloride
in the damp spots replaced a few times a year Ten
minutes walking your property line looking at where the water goes
The dryer vent fixed The air moving And the mold
that is there scrubbed or cut out honestly The
machine will still be in the store waiting for you if you
truly need it But most houses do not need it Most
houses need the water to stop coming in That is the old way
Still works
